fia_partitions.title: FIA state extracts
fia_partitions.blurb: State-partitioned processed FIA extracts, one Parquet file per state. Several are already aggregated rather than raw copies — the tree extract, for instance, is grouped by species, subplot, status, size class, and crown position. These are the working intermediates the national summaries are built from.

fia_summaries.title: FIA national summaries
fia_summaries.blurb: National tables assembled from the state extracts. This is where most researcher-facing FIA work should start.

site_climate.title: Site climate
site_climate.blurb: Monthly TerraClimate values pulled at FIA plot locations.

species_niches.title: Species climate niches
species_niches.blurb: For each tree species, the climate found across its mapped range. Used to ask whether a forest community is made of warm- or cool-associated species.

thermophilization.title: Forest community change
thermophilization.blurb: Finished analysis products measuring whether the climate affinity of a plot's community is shifting between surveys.

ids.title: Insect and Disease Survey
ids.blurb: Aerial survey polygons mapping insect, disease, and other damage.

disturbance_linkage.title: FIA-to-external disturbance linkage
disturbance_linkage.blurb: Planned association between FIA plots and external dated events (MTBS fire severity, IDS damage polygons).

analysis.title: Condition-level analysis
analysis.blurb: Stable-condition histories, cumulative mortality, site climatic water deficit, climate-niche responses, and the current model-ready tables.

climate_grids.title: Gridded climate workflows
climate_grids.blurb: TerraClimate, PRISM, and WorldClim extraction pipelines for IDS geometry.

products.title: FIA condition disturbance and treatment flags
products.one_row_is: one mapped condition within one plot visit
caveats: Neutral per-condition flags, not an analysis population. "Control" vs "disturbed" is deliberately NOT decided here; build it downstream from the flags. Control = is_forested_analysis_condition & !has_any_recorded_disturbance & !has_any_treatment; disturbed = is_forested_analysis_condition & is_natural_disturbance & !is_human_or_harvest & !has_any_treatment.
A "no recorded disturbance" flag means FIA recorded no disturbance code. That is an absence of record, not proof of no event.
is_high_severity_proxy uses crown fire (DSTRBCD 32) as a stand-in for high-severity fire. That choice has not been signed off scientifically.
products.notes: Reusable condition-level disturbance/treatment flags plus raw FIA codes. Filter to whatever population an analysis needs; the repo does not choose control vs disturbed.

products.title: Monthly climate at survey point locations
products.one_row_is: one site, year, month, and climate variable
caveats: These are not all FIA plots. Of the 6,956 sites, 4,886 are tree-ring (ITRDB) locations worldwide and 2,070 are FIA. Filter on `source` in the input location list before treating any subset as an FIA sample.
The FIA sites join on PLT_CN, at the plot-visit level — not stable_plot_id, which matches nothing here.

Joining to this repository's FIA products returns only 198 of the 2,070 FIA sites. The other 1,872 are periodic-inventory visits from 1984-1993, and the processed FIA products start at inventory year 2000 (config.yaml `processed.fia.invyr_min`). This is a coverage mismatch, not a broken key.
FIA coverage is five Interior West states only: MT 910, UT 669, ID 224, CO 156, WY 111.
Values come from the TerraClimate grid cell containing the point, not from the site itself.
Scale factors are already applied. Temperatures are degrees C, water is mm.
Some points snap to ocean or masked cells and return nothing; those are listed in site_climate/qa/outputs/site_climate_missing_sites.csv.
products.notes:
A standalone point extraction, separate from the numbered workflows. It is NOT the output of 05_fia/scripts/site_climate/, whose product is not built in this data root; docs/DATA_PRODUCTS.md records that wrong path for it.
Identifier traced 2026-07-22: all 2,070 FIA site ids match a CN in the raw FIA PLOT tables exactly, so they are genuine PLT_CN values. The periodic inventories they mostly come from are single-year statewide snapshots (MT 1989, UT 1993, ID 1991) and predate the annual inventory design, so comparing them with modern annual-panel plots needs review before use.
"recheck" reads as a scratch directory; promote this to a stable release path before any handoff.

products.title: Seedling community climate change between consecutive surveys
products.one_row_is: one remeasurement interval, for the seedling layer
caveats: A plot measured three times gives two rows. Treating them as independent observations understates how correlated repeat visits are.
Every interval uses FIA's own PREV_PLT_CN remeasurement link. Visits that are merely chronologically adjacent are excluded, not silently paired.
Disturbance columns describe the later visit of the pair. Use fire_within_interval or insect_within_interval to ask whether the dated event falls inside the interval.
rate_ columns divide by the INVYR difference. days_between_measurements gives measured elapsed time when that distinction matters.

products.one_row_is: one mapped damage polygon in one survey year
caveats: Damage sketched from an aircraft. Coverage depends on whether an area was flown that year, so a blank area can mean "no damage" or "not surveyed".
ACRES is the polygon's own reported acreage, not a measure of overlap with anything else.

A handful of rows (6, in 3 identifier groups) share an identifier but disagree on some attribute; they are kept and listed in 01_ids/qa/outputs/damage_areas_identifier_conflicts.csv. They are 0.0001% of the layer and do not materially affect any total.
products.notes:
Lives in a 5.5 GB GeoPackage. The hosted interface must never scan it; requests are handed to a server-side extractor.
Cross-archive duplication fixed and the layer rebuilt 2026-07-23: 4,475,827 -> 4,472,333 rows, total ACRES 587,582,463 -> 542,565,563 (the earlier build double-counted 7.66% of acreage from observations delivered in more than one regional archive). De-duplication lives in scripts/utils/ids_dedupe.R (called from 03_clean_ids.R) with tests in 01_ids/tests/testthat/test_ids_dedupe.R. OBSERVATION_ID + DAMAGE_AREA_ID is now unique except for the 3 attribute-conflict groups noted above.
